title: PRE-REGISTRATION -- COLD extension of the temperature ladder (2026-08-14)
written_before: any SELECTED, oracle@8, sel_eff, distinct-count or EM number existed for ANY of the new cold rungs (T=0.0, 0.05, 0.1, 0.2, 0.4) or for the in-session regenerations (T03r, T05r, T07r). what_is_already_known_and_is_the_basis_o.mechanism: SELECTED = oracle@8 x sel_eff, an EXACT identity (residual 5.55e-17). As T falls, sel_eff rises monotonically and oracle@8 falls; SELECTED is the product. Coverage gains convert at only 0.447 [0.368,0.526]; a proportional sel_eff gain converts at exactly 1.
what_is_already_known_and_is_the_basis_o.the_open_disagreement: In EM currency T=0.3 (+0.01279) beats T=0.5 (+0.00796); in judge currency T=0.5 wins and T=0.3's CI spans zero. The two currencies therefore disagree about WHERE the peak is (not about its sign).

H1_PREDICTED_PEAK.reasoning: the judge currency puts the peak at or above 0.5 and exact match puts it at or below 0.3, so the most likely single location is between them. Mechanistically: below T=0.3 the sel_eff term has at most 0.130 of headroom left (0.8704 -> 1.0 at a fully degenerate pool) while the oracle@8 term still has 0.109 to lose (0.5588 -> the T=0 greedy floor, which the frozen metric puts near 0.4495 for the modal candidate). The product must therefore turn over somewhere in [0.0, 0.3], and the measured curve is already flat between 0.3 and 0.5.
H1_PREDICTED_PEAK.interval_prediction: the peak lies in T in [0.3, 0.5] and SELECTED at T in {0.3, 0.4, 0.5} will be statistically indistinguishable from each other (a PLATEAU, not a sharp peak).
H1_PREDICTED_PEAK.monotonicity_prediction: SELECTED declines monotonically for every T <= 0.2; sel_eff rises monotonically to 1.0 as T -> 0; oracle@8 falls monotonically as T -> 0 and equals the T=0 greedy accuracy exactly at T=0; distinct/8 falls monotonically to exactly 1.000 at T=0.

H2_WHAT_COUNTS_AS_THE_TREND_CONTINUING.definition: SOME rung with T < 0.3 must (a) beat the IN-SESSION T=0.7 control CI-cleanly in BOTH currencies (judge AND normalised exact match, on identical verifier picks), AND (b) have a SELECTED point estimate above BOTH T=0.3 and T=0.5 measured in the same session.
H2_WHAT_COUNTS_AS_THE_TREND_CONTINUING.note: condition (a) alone is not enough -- T=0.3 and T=0.5 already satisfy something like it. The claim being tested is that colder is BETTER STILL, so the new rung must beat the existing best, not merely the control.

H3_WHAT_COUNTS_AS_THE_TREND_TURNING.definition: max SELECTED over T in {0.3, 0.4, 0.5} exceeds the point estimate of every rung with T <= 0.2, AND at least one rung with T <= 0.2 is a CI-clean LOSS versus the in-session control in at least one currency.
H3_WHAT_COUNTS_AS_THE_TREND_TURNING.predicted: THIS is the outcome I expect. Predicted turning region: between T=0.2 and T=0.3.

H4_WHAT_WOULD_KILL_THE_LEVER_ENTIRELY.kill_condition_1: no setting below T=0.7 is CI-clean positive in BOTH currencies against the in-session control -- i.e. the 2026-08-13 T=0.5 win does not reproduce when both arms are regenerated in this session. Then the whole cold-temperature lever is a seed/serving artifact and must be reported as such.
H4_WHAT_WOULD_KILL_THE_LEVER_ENTIRELY.kill_condition_2: the COLLAPSE POINT (below) arrives at or above the peak -- i.e. at the temperature that maximises SELECTED, the verifier's contribution is already indistinguishable from zero. Then the best cold setting is not a best-of-N result at all, it is single-decode with 8x the generation cost, and the lever is dead as a *selection* lever even if the accuracy number is fine.
H4_WHAT_WOULD_KILL_THE_LEVER_ENTIRELY.kill_condition_3: the in-session control itself does not reproduce the frozen bar within the project's stated +-0.008 open-text reproducibility band.

H5_THE_COLLAPSE_POINT_DEFINITION_fixed_i.primary_statistic: VC_single(T) = SELECTED(T) - RANDOM_SLOT(T), where RANDOM_SLOT is the EXACT expectation of drawing one of the 8 samples uniformly at random from the SAME pool (computed as the per-item mean of the 8 slot labels, then averaged over items). This is 'what best-of-8 buys you over paying 1/8 of the generation cost at the same temperature'. Paired item bootstrap, n=2345, nboot=10000, seed 20260814.
H5_THE_COLLAPSE_POINT_DEFINITION_fixed_i.secondary_statistic: VC_modal(T) = SELECTED(T) - MODAL_VOTE(T), where MODAL_VOTE is the frozen metric's `greedy` field = the judge/EM label of the pool's modal (majority-vote) candidate. Majority vote is itself a training-free selector, so this is the harder bar; it is reported alongside, not instead.
H5_THE_COLLAPSE_POINT_DEFINITION_fixed_i.collapse_point_readout: the collapse point is reported as the bracketing interval (T_coldest_still_CI_clean, T_warmest_not_CI_clean) on the primary statistic, in BOTH currencies. Because the ladder is discrete, no interpolation will be performed and no single T will be quoted as 'the' collapse point unless a rung lands exactly on it.
H5_THE_COLLAPSE_POINT_DEFINITION_fixed_i.degeneracy_readout: distinct-candidate count per rung (mean over items of the number of distinct normalised candidate strings in the 8-pool) and the fraction of items with exactly 1 distinct candidate (the UNANIMOUS stratum, on which sel_eff is 1.0 for every selector by construction and the verifier has no choice to make).
H5_THE_COLLAPSE_POINT_DEFINITION_fixed_i.T0_special_case: vLLM 0.10.1.1 REFUSES n>1 at temperature 0 ('ValueError: n must be 1 when using greedy sampling, got 8.', measured 2026-08-14 07:14 UTC). T=0.0 is therefore generated at n=1, three times with three different seeds. If all three seeds agree byte-for-byte on all 2345 items, that is a MEASUREMENT that argmax decoding is deterministic here, and it licenses the statement that the 8-sample pool at T=0 contains exactly 1 distinct candidate. No replicated draw will be written to disk or counted as a sample: the frozen metric handles a 1-slot pool correctly on its own (unfilled slots score MISSING_SCORE, argmax picks slot 0, oracle = greedy = selected, sel_eff = 1.0).

H6_HOW_THE_JUDGE_VS_EM_DISAGREEMENT_WILL.rule_0: both currencies are computed on IDENTICAL verifier picks (genframe_data.sel_eff(...)['picks']), so they can differ ONLY in the label applied to the picked slot.
H6_HOW_THE_JUDGE_VS_EM_DISAGREEMENT_WILL.rule_1_sign: a rung is called a WIN only if it is CI-clean positive in BOTH currencies (the classification the 2026-08-14 finalize step already uses). A CI-clean win in one currency and a CI-clean loss in the other is a CURRENCY CONFLICT and is reported as a grading effect, never as an accuracy result.
H6_HOW_THE_JUDGE_VS_EM_DISAGREEMENT_WILL.rule_2_peak_location: if the two currencies disagree about WHICH rung is the peak (rather than about the sign), the tie-break is MECHANISTIC, not a vote: (i) audit the mean generated-token count of the PICKED slot per rung. The judge prompt instructs it to 'be lenient about phrasing, synonyms, and abbreviations', and this project has already caught repetition_penalty=1.10 harvesting that leniency with verbosity. If the judge-favoured rung's picked answers are systematically longer, the judge gap is attributed to leniency and EXACT MATCH is preferred. (ii) if picked-slot token length is matched within +-1 token between the two candidate peaks, the disagreement is declared NOISE and the peak is reported as an interval covering both rungs -- not resolved in favour of either. (iii) additionally report the judge-minus-EM disagreement RATE on the picked slot per rung; if that rate is flat across the ladder, no leniency mechanism is available to explain the gap and (ii) applies.
H6_HOW_THE_JUDGE_VS_EM_DISAGREEMENT_WILL.rule_3: if no single rung is the peak in both currencies, the reported answer is 'the peak is a PLATEAU over {T...}', stated as such rather than resolved.

H7_N_INTERACTION_PREDICTION.prediction: at cold temperatures the 8-pool is redundant, so SELECTED(N=4) will be within noise of SELECTED(N=8) for every T <= 0.3, while at the deployed T=0.7 there will be a visible N=4 -> N=8 gap. Consequence, if it holds: cold + N=4 matches deployed hot + N=8 at ~2x lower generation cost.
H7_N_INTERACTION_PREDICTION.secondary_prediction: at T <= 0.2, even N=2 will be within noise of N=8, because the mean distinct-candidate count will already be under ~1.6.
H7_N_INTERACTION_PREDICTION.method: subsample the EXISTING 8-sample pools -- exact hypergeometric expectation where a closed form exists (oracle@N), and seed-averaged random subsets for SELECTED (which depends on which slots are present, so it is averaged over subsets). No new generation.

H8_CONNECTION_TO_THE_RESOLUTION_LIMIT.known: artifacts/resolution_sweep_2026-08-13.json: ONE GREEDY DECODE AT NATIVE RESOLUTION scores 0.486994 and TIES the deployed 8-sample cap320 + verifier arm at 0.482871, at 0.0759x its FLOPs.
H8_CONNECTION_TO_THE_RESOLUTION_LIMIT.prediction: the T=0.0 rung measured HERE is the cap320-matched version of that comparison, and I predict it does NOT tie: cap320 greedy will land near 0.45-0.46 and be a CI-clean LOSS against the in-session 8-sample T=0.7 control. That would establish that the native-resolution tie is a RESOLUTION effect, not a 'stop sampling' effect -- the two are separable and only one of them is free.
H8_CONNECTION_TO_THE_RESOLUTION_LIMIT.falsifier: if cap320 T=0.0 greedy ties the in-session control, then sampling buys nothing at ANY temperature and the honest recommendation is to stop sampling. That outcome will be reported plainly as the headline if it occurs.
